column1: # MONEY rules (ADR-0008 §5, rules-money-v1). Format: see FactFixtures.kt.
# Not markers in v1 (ADR-0008 §5.3): C$, Rs, ¢
# Multi-code symbols without context: currency null, the symbol as printed
# Symbol and code on the same digits
# English-word codes alone need printed fraction digits (ZZ-04)
# A zero first group cannot be a grouping (review E-10, ruling Q11)
# First group over 3 digits: no grouping reading, abstained (ruling Q11)
# A bare number is never money; no marker, no claim
# E-01: ASCII-space groups keep every printed zero
# E-04: dash look-alikes and spaced signs abstain (ruling Q10); a plain '-' touching the amount is a sign
# E-07: a range claims both markers
# E-06: format and combining marks attach; never a boundary
# E-08: any space separator between a marker and its digits
# E-10, Q11: a single separator before 3 digits whose grouping reading is impossible
# E-10: a code beside a signed number is never context
# EE-01: a + run of 7-15 digits beside a free marker is phone or money: abstained as PHONE
# EE-02: a space-grouped amount with a fraction abstains whole, prefix and suffix alike
# EE-02 / A-8: any single space separator splitting a number groups like an ASCII space
# EE-04: a mark leading or inside an amount abstains visibly, covering the mark
# EE-05: a second sign or a plus-minus abstains
# EE-06: zero-led groups; the first group stands in for a zero-led adjacent group
# Residual rulings: currency pairs and credit markers
# P3-06 follow-up F3 (proposed A-14): a dash attached to a preceding letter is a separator, not a sign.
# The sign is unclaimed, so the amount abstains (SIGN_OR_CREDIT); no negative or positive definite value.
# Controls: a sign after space, a symbol or at the start stays a sign (unchanged)
